Importing the Necessary Libraries

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
#Data from Jan 1st-Nov 15th 2026
housing_data_2025 = 
  read_csv(
    "data/Housing_Maintenance_code_Violations_2026.csv",
    na = c("NA", ".", ""),
    show_col_types = FALSE
  ) |> 
  janitor::clean_names() 

#Data from Jan 1st-Nov 15th 2025
housing_data_2026 = 
  read_csv(
    "data/Housing_Maintenance_Code_Violations_2025.csv",
    na = c("NA", ".", ""),
    show_col_types = FALSE
  ) |> 
  janitor::clean_names() 

```


Now that we've imported our data, we are going to need a few helper functions to process it.

```{r}
#For the date, not to add too many unnecessary columns, we create a helper function to get the day, month, and year from date notation
get_date = function(date){
  full_date = myd(date)
  date_df = tibble(
    day = day(full_date),
    month = month(full_date),
    year = year(full_date)
  )
  return(date_df)
}

```
